## Overview

`PhyloCactus` is an R package for assembling, curating and analyzing multilocus sequence datasets built from public DNA sequences. It covers sequence retrieval from GenBank, quality control, phylogenetic inference, divergence time estimation, visualization and comparison with published phylogenies.

Multilocus matrices assembled from GenBank inherit the heterogeneity of decades of deposition: inconsistent locus annotations, duplicated accessions, records without vouchers, orthographic variants and nomenclatural synonyms. Converting these records into a phylogenetic matrix requires curation, taxonomic reconciliation against an accepted checklist, and quality control of each alignment. The difficulty increases in plant lineages that diversified recently and rapidly, where low plastid divergence, incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) and reticulate evolution increase the risk of erroneous orthology assessment and of alignment error.

**Cactaceae**, one of the largest succulent radiations of the Neotropics (Arakaki *et al*. 2011; Hernández-Hernández *et al*. 2014; Guerrero *et al*. 2019), combine these properties, and their GenBank record is uneven in taxonomic and locus coverage. `PhyloCactus` was developed on this family and implements its assembly and analysis as a reproducible workflow.

## Design

Each analytical step relies on established software, but chaining those programs by hand requires ad hoc scripts in which parameters, intermediate files and decisions are easily lost. `PhyloCactus` wraps each step in a function with explicit arguments and documented outputs, and the outputs of one module are the inputs of the next. Every module writes its parameters and results to disk, so that an analysis can be traced from the retrieved sequences to the final chronogram and resumed from any completed module.

## Workflow

The workflow comprises thirteen modules grouped in four stages.

```{r workflow-fig, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Conceptual framework of the PhyloCactus pipeline"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/Fig1_PhyloCactus_Workflow.png") 
```

1. **Data Assembly and Preparation (Modules 1 to 6)**: retrieval of orthologous sequence clusters with `phylotaR`, alignment with `MAFFT`, masking of unreliable alignment regions with `DECIPHER`, a saturation screen, taxonomic reconciliation against the Caryophyllales.org checklist (`CactaceaeFullList_2026_07_01_Beatriz_Merino.xlsx`; Korotkova *et al*. 2021), and concatenation into a partitioned supermatrix.
2. **Phylogenetic Inference and Dating (Modules 7 to 10)**: substitution model selection per partition with `ModelTest-NG` under AICc, constrained maximum-likelihood inference with `RAxML-NG`, Felsenstein bootstrap proportions (FBP) with the transfer bootstrap expectation (TBE) as a secondary measure, temporal bootstrap replicates, and penalized likelihood dating with `treePL`.
3. **Visualization and Metadata Integration (Modules 11 and 12)**: IUCN Red List assessments retrieved with `rredlist`, collapse of nodes with FBP < 0.70 into polytomies, and tree, chronogram and conservation figures.
4. **Validation (Module 13)**: Robinson-Foulds and information-theoretic distances and multidimensional scaling (MDS) of tree space (`validate_phylogenies()`) against published phylogenies, one of which can optionally be summarized from published gene trees under the multispecies coalescent with `ASTRAL-III`.

Each stage can be run on its own, from the outputs of the previous one.

## Installation

### Install PhyloCactus

Install the development version directly from GitHub:

``` r
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github("beeamerino/PhyloCactus")
```

Verify that the package has been installed:

``` r
library(PhyloCactus)

packageVersion("PhyloCactus")
```

### R Package Dependencies

`PhyloCactus` depends on packages from CRAN, Bioconductor and GitHub:

| Repository | Main packages |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **GitHub** | `phylotaR` |
| **Bioconductor** | `DECIPHER`, `Biostrings`, `ggtree` |
| **CRAN** | `ape`, `phangorn`, `TreeDist`, `ggplot2`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `stringr`, `purrr`, `rredlist` |

Install the Bioconductor packages with:

``` r
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install(c("DECIPHER", "Biostrings", "ggtree"))
```

#### phylotaR

[`phylotaR`](https://github.com/ropensci/phylotaR) (Bennett *et al.* 2018) retrieves orthologous DNA sequences from GenBank by BLAST-based clustering, which does not depend on the gene names given in the records. Install it from GitHub:

``` r
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github('ropensci/phylotaR')
```

#### blastula (optional)

[`blastula`](https://github.com/rstudio/blastula) is used only to send an email when a long analysis
running on the local machine ends. `automate_treePL()` accepts `notify = TRUE`
for that, and `send_run_notification()` can be called from any script. It is a suggested
dependency, not a required one, so `PhyloCactus` installs and runs without it; the only difference
is that the notification reports on the console that it is sending nothing. Install it from CRAN if
you want it:

``` r
install.packages("blastula")
```

Two things are configured outside the package, and neither is ever read by `PhyloCactus`:

``` r
usethis::edit_r_environ()   # add: MY_EMAIL=you@example.org

blastula::create_smtp_creds_file(
  file = "~/.blastula_gmail",
  user = "you@example.org",
  provider = "gmail"
)
```

For a Gmail account, use an application password, not the account password. The
credentials file belongs outside any repository, and `PhyloCactus` only hands its path to
`blastula`. Set `PHYLOCACTUS_SMTP_CREDS` in your `.Renviron` to keep it somewhere other than
`~/.blastula_gmail`.

## External Software

The following command-line programs must be installed separately and available on the system `PATH`:

| Software | Purpose | Citation |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|
| [`BLAST+`](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279690/) | Sequence similarity search for cluster identification | Camacho, C. *et al*. (2009). BLAST+: Architecture and applications. *BMC Bioinformatics*, 10. <https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-10-421> |
| [`MAFFT`](https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/) | Multiple sequence alignment | Katoh, K., & Standley, D. M. (2013). MAFFT multiple sequence alignment software version 7: Improvements in performance and usability. *Molecular Biology and Evolution*, 30(4), 772–780. <https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/mst010> |
| [`ModelTest-NG`](https://github.com/ddarriba/modeltest) | Model selection | Darriba, D. *et al*. (2020). ModelTest-NG: a new and scalable tool for the selection of DNA and protein evolutionary models. *Molecular Biology and Evolution*, 37(1), 291-294. <https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msz189> |
| [`RAxML-NG`](https://github.com/amkozlov/raxml-ng) | Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference | Kozlov, A. M. *et al*. (2019). RAxML-NG: A fast, scalable and user-friendly tool for maximum likelihood phylogenetic inference. *Bioinformatics*, 35(21), 4453–4455. <https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btz305> |
| [`treePL`](https://github.com/blackrim/treePL) | Divergence time estimation | Smith, S. A., & O’Meara, B. C. (2012). TreePL: Divergence time estimation using penalized likelihood for large phylogenies. *Bioinformatics*, 28(20), 2689–2690. <https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bts492> |

### Configuring the System PATH

If R does not find an executable, add its installation directory to `PATH` in `.Renviron`:

``` r
usethis::edit_r_environ()
```

For example:

``` bash
PATH="/Users/**your_user**/miniconda3/bin:${PATH}"
```

Restart the R session after saving the file.

## Package Structure

Each function performs one analytical task, and its outputs are the documented inputs of the next module. Individual modules can therefore be used in other workflows, analyses can be resumed from intermediate stages, and each stage writes its own log files.

## Typical Output Structure

Each module writes to its own numbered directory: FASTA files, alignments, metadata tables, partition files, trees in Newick or NEXUS format, and summary reports. A completed module does not need to be repeated when a later one is rerun.

## Next Steps

With `PhyloCactus` and its external dependencies installed, continue with [Tutorial 1: Data Assembly and Preparation](https://beeamerino.github.io/PhyloCactus/articles/tutorial-1-cactus-phylogeny-prep.html), which assembles a curated multilocus dataset from GenBank.
